chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba, from Asbat ibn Salim, from Israil ibn Abu Usama al-Baya' al-Zutti, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The example of the violet (oil) among the oils is like our example among the people.

key_terms.الْبَنَفْسَجِ: violet (a type of flower used for fragrant oil)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith comparing the Ahl al-Bayt to violet oil?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the metaphor of violet oil (*banafsj*)—a precious, aromatic essence extracted from flowers and distinct from common base oils—to illustrate the unique spiritual purity and elevated status of the Ahl al-Bayt among humanity. This imagery underscores their role as the refined essence of prophetic guidance, distinguishing them from the general populace just as violet oil stands apart from ordinary perfumes. The metaphor highlights both their intrinsic nobility and their function as a source of spiritual fragrance and healing for the community.
